purpose: Source-validated evidence of pedagogical quality, continuity and disciplinary breadth across the history of the Bécsi Magyar Iskola. Historical roles and qualifications are tied to their source date and do not imply continuous employment.

institutionalClaim.claim: Across multiple documented eras since 1987, BMI has repeatedly worked with qualified, university-educated and specialist educators. The evidence supports an institution-level characterization of a highly qualified, experienced and pedagogically diverse educator network.
institutionalClaim.limits: This does not mean every historical contributor held a university degree, regulated title or identical qualification level. Exact qualifications remain person-specific and source-bound.

historicalPedagogicalMilestones.roleEvidence: Founders associated with the start of Hungarian mother-tongue education in Vienna and the early school community.
The jubilee publication documents a Hungarian and English secondary-teacher degree, earlier Hungarian language and literature teaching, and BMI teaching from 2006.
The jubilee publication documents a Hungarian and English secondary-teacher degree, many years of teaching experience, BMI teaching from 2010 and development of Hungarian heritage-language materials.

The school documented academic and general leadership, framework-curriculum and pedagogical leadership, coordination and cultural-program responsibility, together with an independent scientific advisory body.
pedagogicalEvidence: qualified preschool educators, primary teachers and teachers working under a shared concept
differentiated instruction based on pupils' Hungarian-language competence
methods explicitly informed by bilingualism research

historicalPedagogicalMilestones.roleEvidence: The 30-year jubilee publication explicitly lists these educators as contributors to BMI's successful work between 2012 and 2017.

The jubilee volume contains individual qualification and biography evidence spanning secondary teaching, preschool and primary teaching, university teaching, music pedagogy, music therapy, Waldorf pedagogy, heritage-language teaching, Hungarian-as-a-foreign-language teaching, mathematics and academic leadership.

Current canonical profile documents more than thirty years in pedagogy, Austrian teaching and special-education experience, Hungarian preschool and primary-teacher qualifications, Austrian special-education qualification, Montessori diploma and motopedagogy certification; BMI Hungarian-language teaching since 2012.
Current and press sources document long-term pedagogical involvement connected with BMI; Kiss Ágnes in Hungarian-language teaching and Boronkai Gabriella in visual, movement and children's programs.

currentDocumentedPedagogicalBreadth.interpretation: The current profiles support a multidisciplinary expert network. Each person's exact current role and qualification must be taken from the canonical profile.

qualityIndicators: university and teacher-training degrees documented for multiple educators
formal preschool-teacher, primary-teacher and special-education qualifications
Montessori, motopedagogy, Waldorf, speech/language-development and other specialist training
academic participation in curriculum and didactic design
explicit use of bilingualism research and differentiated heritage-language instruction
source-grounded historical educator roster and external press corroboration
conflictRule: The jubilee publication contains both an explicit September 1987 start statement and a later narrative sentence referring to a 1988 restart. Canonical founding remains 1987-09 because the explicit start statement aligns with stronger external corroboration.

safetyRules.employment: Teaching, coordination, advisory or program activity does not by itself establish employment status.
safetyRules.credential: Only assert regulated credentials when explicitly supported by a canonical profile, the public jubilee PDF or another qualified source.
safetyRules.quality: The phrase 'highly qualified educator network' is permitted as a qualitative institution-level characterization because multiple individual university degrees, teaching qualifications, specialist credentials and long professional careers are documented. It must not be converted into a ranking or universal claim about every historical contributor.
